tests.title: reset-to-origin rejects a request with no credential before touching git or the database
given: a registered carry_patch workspace and patch
tests.when: POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin is called with no Authorization header
then: the status is 401
the body carries an authentication-required error
no git command is invoked and no row is updated
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url, auth=nil); assert r.status == 401; assert gitRunner.calls == 0

tests.title: reset-to-origin rejects a PAT lacking patches:write before touching git or the database
given: a PAT credential with scopes not including patches:write
tests.when: POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin is called with that PAT
then: the status is 403
the body carries a missing-scope error
no git command is invoked and no row is updated
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url, auth=patWithoutScope); assert r.status == 403; assert gitRunner.calls == 0

tests.title: reset-to-origin returns the same 404 for a nonexistent workspace and a non-owner's workspace
given: workspace A owned by user 1
an authenticated user 2 with no admin token
tests.when: user 2 calls reset-to-origin on workspace A's slug, and separately on a slug that does not exist
then: both responses are 404 with the identical body shape
no patch or git state changes
tests.pseudocode: r1 = post(urlFor('workspace-a'), auth=user2); r2 = post(urlFor('no-such-slug'), auth=user2); assert r1.status == r2.status == 404; assert r1.body == r2.body_shape

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a non-carry_patch workspace
given: a hub-mode (non carry_patch) workspace owned by the caller
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called against it
then: the status is 400
the message is 'reset-to-origin is only supported for carry_patch workspaces'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'reset-to-origin is only supported for carry_patch workspaces'

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a workspace that is not active
given: a carry_patch workspace with status archived
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called against it
then: the status is 400
the message is 'workspace is not active'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'workspace is not active'

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a workspace whose clone is not ready
given: a carry_patch, active workspace with clone_status 'cloning'
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called against it
then: the status is 400
the message is 'workspace clone is not ready'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'workspace clone is not ready'

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a workspace whose PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is not 'origin'
given: a carry_patch, active, ready workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset (defaulting to hub)
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called against it
then: the status is 400
the message is 'reset-to-origin requires PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin'
the error type is patch_branch_source_mismatch
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'reset-to-origin requires PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin'; assert r.body.type == 'patch_branch_source_mismatch'

tests.title: reset-to-origin proceeds identically regardless of PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY value
given: a workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin passing every other gate
tests.when: for any value of PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY (replace, report, unset)
then: the endpoint proceeds to perform the same replace and never reads or branches on PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY
tests.pseudocode: for policy in ['replace','report','']: setVar('PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY', policy); r = post(url); assert r.status == 200; assert getVariableCalls.excludes('PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY')

tests.title: reset-to-origin returns 404 for a patch id not found in the given slug's workspace, including cross-workspace ids
given: a patch belonging to workspace B
tests.when: POST /workspaces/A/patches/:id/reset-to-origin is called using workspace B's patch id under slug A
then: the status is 404
the message is 'patch not found'
tests.pseudocode: r = post('/workspaces/A/patches/' + patchOfB.id + '/reset-to-origin'); assert r.status == 404; assert r.body.error == 'patch not found'

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a soft-deleted patch
given: a patch with status 'deleted'
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called for that patch
then: the status is 409
the message is 'patch is soft-deleted; restore it first'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 409; assert r.body.error == 'patch is soft-deleted; restore it first'

tests.title: reset-to-origin refuses a patch whose branch_name equals the integration branch
given: a patch row whose branch_name has been made equal to the workspace's integration_branch
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called for that patch
then: the status is 400
the message is 'cannot reset the integration branch'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'cannot reset the integration branch'

tests.title: reset-to-origin proceeds to the reset for any eligible patch status
given: a patch whose local and origin branches both exist and differ
tests.when: for any status in {active, conflict, disabled, merged_upstream}
then: the endpoint proceeds to the reset operation and returns 200
tests.pseudocode: for st in ['active','conflict','disabled','merged_upstream']: setStatus(patch, st); r = post(url); assert r.status == 200

tests.title: reset-to-origin returns workspace_busy when the workspace lock is held and touches no ref
given: wslock.TryLock(slug) is made to fail by holding the lock externally
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called
then: the status is 409
the message is 'workspace_busy'
no ref is read or written
tests.pseudocode: wslock.hold(slug); r = post(url); assert r.status == 409; assert r.body.error == 'workspace_busy'; assert gitRunner.refCalls == 0

tests.title: reset-to-origin fails with a clear message when refs/remotes/origin/<branch> is missing, without fetching or writing
given: a trunk with no refs/remotes/origin/<branch> for the patch's branch
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called
then: the status is 400
the message is 'branch not found on origin; sync the workspace first'
no fetch command and no update-ref call occurred
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body.error == 'branch not found on origin; sync the workspace first'; assert gitRunner.notCalled('fetch'); assert gitRunner.notCalled('update-ref')

tests.title: reset-to-origin backs up the existing local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch> before moving it, overwriting an earlier backup
given: refs/heads/<branch> exists at SHA old1
refs/hub/replaced/<branch> already exists at some earlier SHA
refs/remotes/origin/<branch> exists at SHA new1
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called
then: refs/hub/replaced/<branch> now reads old1 (overwriting the earlier value)
the response body includes replaced_sha == old1
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert git.revParse('refs/hub/replaced/'+branch) == old1; assert r.body.replaced_sha == old1

tests.title: reset-to-origin skips the backup and creates the local branch directly at the origin tip when no local branch exists
given: refs/heads/<branch> does not exist in the trunk
refs/remotes/origin/<branch> exists at SHA new1
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called
then: refs/hub/replaced/<branch> is not written
refs/heads/<branch> now exists at new1
the response body omits replaced_sha entirely
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert not git.refExists('refs/hub/replaced/'+branch); assert git.revParse(branch) == new1; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.body

tests.title: reset-to-origin always moves the local branch to the origin tip via update-ref, even when already equal
given: refs/remotes/origin/<branch> exists at SHA new1
tests.when: for any starting value of refs/heads/<branch> (absent, equal to new1, or different from new1)
then: after the call refs/heads/<branch> equals new1
the move was performed with update-ref and never with checkout or reset
tests.pseudocode: for start in [None, new1, old1]: setLocalBranch(branch, start); r = post(url); assert git.revParse(branch) == new1; assert gitRunner.notCalled('checkout'); assert gitRunner.notCalled('reset', excluding='HardReset-when-checked-out')

tests.title: reset-to-origin hard-resets the working tree when the reset branch is the trunk's current checkout
given: git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD in the trunk reports <branch>
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called and moves <branch> to the origin tip
then: HardReset is invoked on the trunk with the new tip immediately after the ref move
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert gitRunner.hardResetCalls == [newTip]

tests.title: reset-to-origin does not hard-reset the working tree when a different branch is checked out
given: git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD in the trunk reports a branch other than <branch>
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin is called and moves <branch> to the origin tip
then: HardReset is not invoked
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert gitRunner.hardResetCalls == []

tests.title: reset-to-origin updates origin_sync_state, origin_sha, and origin_synced_at while leaving other patch fields untouched
given: a patch row with status conflict, position 2, description 'x', upstream_pr_url 'y'
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin completes successfully
then: origin_sync_state is 'in_sync'
origin_sha equals the origin tip
origin_synced_at is set to a recent timestamp
status remains conflict, position remains 2, description remains 'x', upstream_pr_url remains 'y'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); row = readPatchRow(id); assert row.origin_sync_state=='in_sync'; assert row.origin_sha==newTip; assert row.status=='conflict'; assert row.position==2; assert row.description=='x'

tests.title: reset-to-origin emits one hub.patch.replace audit event attributed to the calling credential
given: a patch with a preexisting local branch, called by API key user 'alice'
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin completes successfully
then: exactly one hub.patch.replace audit event is emitted
it carries the branch name, the discarded local SHA, and the new origin SHA
its actor is 'alice', not 'system'
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url, auth=alice); events = audit.emitted('hub.patch.replace'); assert len(events)==1; assert events[0].actor=='alice'; assert events[0].metadata.old_sha==old1; assert events[0].metadata.new_sha==newTip

tests.title: reset-to-origin responds with the patch record in the shared JSON shape including origin_sync fields
given: a patch eligible for reset
tests.when: POST reset-to-origin succeeds
then: the status is 200
the body includes id, branch_name, status, origin_sync_state, origin_sha, origin_synced_at matching what GET and PATCH .../patches already return
tests.pseudocode: r = post(url); assert r.status==200; assert set(['id','branch_name','status','origin_sync_state','origin_sha','origin_synced_at']).issubset(r.body.keys())

tests.title: reset-to-origin's response is built from a direct query against the patches table, not from internal/workspace's response helper
given: a mock DB and no dependency on internal/workspace's patchResponse
tests.when: handleResetToOrigin builds the response body
then: the handler issues a SELECT against the patches table itself and does not call any exported/unexported function from internal/workspace
tests.pseudocode: assert callGraph(handleResetToOrigin).doesNotCall('workspace.patchResponse'); assert db.queriesExecuted.includes('SELECT * FROM patches WHERE id = ?')

tests.title: afc patch reset-to-origin sends the endpoint with no body and prints the returned patch JSON, exiting 0
given: a running hub API returning 200 with a patch body for reset-to-origin
tests.when: afc patch reset-to-origin ws-slug patch-id is run
then: the HTTP request body is empty
stdout carries the patch JSON in the same shape as afc patch restore
the process exits 0
tests.pseudocode: result = runCLI(['patch','reset-to-origin','ws-slug','patch-id']); assert result.exitCode==0; assert json.loads(result.stdout)['id']=='patch-id'; assert lastRequest.body==''

tests.title: afc patch reset-to-origin exits 1 on any non-2xx response
given: a running hub API stubbed to return each of: 404 patch not found, 404 workspace not found, 400 patch_branch_source_mismatch, 400 branch not found on origin, 409 soft-deleted patch, 409 workspace_busy, and a network error
tests.when: afc patch reset-to-origin ws-slug patch-id is run against each
then: every invocation prints the error and exits 1
tests.pseudocode: for resp in responses: result = runCLI(['patch','reset-to-origin','ws-slug','patch-id'], stub=resp); assert result.exitCode==1

tests.title: afc patch reset-to-origin accepts exactly two positional args and no request-body flags
given: the afc CLI command tree
tests.when: the reset-to-origin subcommand's flag set and argument arity are inspected
then: exactly two positional arguments are required (workspace-slug, patch-id)
no body-carrying flags are defined, matching afc patch restore's shape
tests.pseudocode: cmd = findCommand('patch','reset-to-origin'); assert cmd.Args == cobra.ExactArgs(2); assert cmd.Flags().bodyFlags == []

tests.title: an existing refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref is advertised and fetchable like any other ref
given: a trunk containing refs/hub/replaced/feature-x at some SHA
tests.when: a client performs git fetch <hub-url> refs/hub/replaced/feature-x
then: the ref is present in the advertisement
the fetch succeeds and yields the backed-up SHA, with no API or shell access used
tests.pseudocode: adv = writeRefAdvertisement(trunk); assert 'refs/hub/replaced/feature-x' in adv.References; fetched = gitFetch(hubURL, 'refs/hub/replaced/feature-x'); assert fetched == expectedSHA

tests.title: the git server rejects any push whose target ref matches refs/hub/replaced/*, unconditionally
given: a workspace in each combination of workspace_mode and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE
a client attempting git push <hub-url> HEAD:refs/hub/replaced/feature-x
tests.when: the push is executed against the receive-pack endpoint
then: the ref update is rejected (reported ng) with message 'refs/hub/replaced/* is a hub-managed backup namespace and cannot be pushed to'
the ref's value in the trunk is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for mode,src in combos: result = gitPush(hubURL, 'HEAD:refs/hub/replaced/feature-x'); assert result.refStatus('refs/hub/replaced/feature-x') == ('ng', 'refs/hub/replaced/* is a hub-managed backup namespace and cannot be pushed to'); assert git.revParse('refs/hub/replaced/feature-x') == before

tests.title: a push containing both a rejected backup-ref target and other legitimate ref updates applies the other updates
given: a push updating both refs/hub/replaced/feature-x and refs/heads/other-branch
tests.when: the push is executed
then: refs/hub/replaced/feature-x is rejected
refs/heads/other-branch is updated normally in the same push
tests.pseudocode: result = gitPush(hubURL, ['HEAD:refs/hub/replaced/feature-x', 'HEAD:refs/heads/other-branch']); assert result.refStatus('refs/hub/replaced/feature-x')[0]=='ng'; assert result.refStatus('refs/heads/other-branch')[0]=='ok'; assert git.revParse('other-branch')==pushedSHA

tests.title: hard-deleting a patch calls the registered backup-ref cleanup hook which best-effort deletes the backup ref
given: a patch with an existing refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref
a registered cleanup hook via the same style as RegisterBranchCheckHook
tests.when: DELETE /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id (and afc patch remove) hard-deletes the row
then: the cleanup hook is invoked with (slug, branchName) after the row is removed
refs/hub/replaced/<branch> no longer exists
the delete response is unaffected by the hook's outcome
tests.pseudocode: hookCalls=[]; RegisterCleanupHook(lambda s,b: hookCalls.append((s,b)) or deleteRef(s,b)); r = deletePatch(slug, id); assert r.status==200; assert hookCalls==[(slug, branch)]; assert not git.refExists('refs/hub/replaced/'+branch)

tests.title: a cleanup hook error during hard-delete is logged, not raised, and the delete still succeeds
given: a registered cleanup hook that returns an error (e.g. trunk missing)
tests.when: DELETE /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id is called
then: the delete response is still 200
the error is logged, not propagated to the caller
tests.pseudocode: RegisterCleanupHook(lambda s,b: raise Error('no trunk')); r = deletePatch(slug, id); assert r.status==200; assert logContains('no trunk')

tests.title: PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches resolves workspace slug and branch name before removing each row and deletes the corresponding backup ref
given: two soft-deleted patch rows past retention, each with a refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref in their workspace's trunk
a WorkspaceRoot and NewGitRunner factory threaded through
tests.when: PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store, workspaceRoot, newGitRunner) runs
then: both rows are purged from the database
both corresponding refs/hub/replaced/<branch> refs are deleted from their trunks
tests.pseudocode: count, err = PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store, root, newGitRunner); assert err==nil; assert count==2; for row in rows: assert not git.refExists(root, row.slug, 'refs/hub/replaced/'+row.branch)

tests.title: PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches continues purging remaining rows and returns an unaffected count when a trunk cannot be opened
given: two purge-eligible rows, one whose workspace trunk directory has been removed (archived), one with a normal trunk
tests.when: PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches runs
then: the error opening the archived workspace's trunk is logged, not raised
both database rows are still purged (count == 2)
the healthy row's backup ref is still deleted
tests.pseudocode: count, err = PurgeExpiredDeletedPatches(ctx, store, root, newGitRunner); assert err==nil; assert count==2; assert logContains('trunk'); assert not git.refExists(root, healthyRow.slug, 'refs/hub/replaced/'+healthyRow.branch)

tests.title: patch-status computes replaced_sha per patch via one rev-parse --verify when NewGitRunner opens successfully
given: a workspace with two patches, one with an existing refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref and one without

tests.when: GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status is called

exactly one rev-parse --verify call was made per patch
tests.pseudocode: r = get('/patch-status'); entry = findEntry(r.body.patches, patchWithBackup.id); assert entry.replaced_sha == backupSHA; assert gitRunner.revParseCalls == len(patches)

tests.title: PatchStatusAPIConfig exposes a NewGitRunner field wired to the shared carry-patch git runner factory in main.go
given: main.go's wiring of RegisterPatchStatusRoutes
tests.when: the PatchStatusAPIConfig passed to RegisterPatchStatusRoutes is inspected
then: its NewGitRunner field is set to the same cpGitRunnerFactory used by every other carry-patch endpoint
tests.pseudocode: cfg = wiredPatchStatusConfig(); assert cfg.NewGitRunner == cpGitRunnerFactory

tests.title: patch-status leaves replaced_sha absent for every patch and still returns 200 when NewGitRunner is nil
given: a PatchStatusAPIConfig with NewGitRunner left nil, as existing tests construct it
tests.when: GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status is called

no patch entry carries replaced_sha

tests.title: patch-status leaves replaced_sha absent for every patch and still returns 200 when opening the runner fails
given: a PatchStatusAPIConfig with NewGitRunner returning an error (e.g. clone not ready)

tests.title: patch-status omits replaced_sha entirely for a patch with no backup ref
given: a patch with no refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref in the trunk
a working NewGitRunner
tests.when: GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status is called
then: that patch's JSON object carries no replaced_sha key
tests.pseudocode: r = get('/patch-status'); entry = findEntry(r.body.patches, patch.id); assert 'replaced_sha' not in entry

tests.title: afc workspace sync exposes a --fail-on-diverged boolean flag defaulting to false

tests.title: afc workspace sync --fail-on-diverged exits 3 immediately after printing the response, before any --wait polling

the process exits with code 3
no rebuild-status poll request is issued

tests.title: afc workspace sync exits 0 when --fail-on-diverged is absent, or patches_diverged is absent or empty
given: stubbed sync responses: (a) no --fail-on-diverged flag with patches_diverged non-empty, (b) --fail-on-diverged with patches_diverged absent, (c) --fail-on-diverged with patches_diverged empty

tests.title: exit code 3 from afc workspace sync is reserved exclusively for the diverged-patches case
given: a stubbed sync failure response unrelated to divergence (e.g. workspace not found)

tests.title: the workflow guide's Getting Started, conflict-resolution, Day-to-day, and API reference sections describe the new fork-authoritative-first flow and recovery surface
given: docs/carry_patch_workflow.md
tests.when: the document is parsed for its Getting Started, 'Resolving conflicts after a failed rebuild', Day-to-day operations, and API reference summary table sections
then: Getting Started presents PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin + push-to-fork + afc patch add + afc workspace sync as the primary path with hub-push labelled as the alternative
the conflict-resolution section documents an origin-mode variant noting rerere will not record fixes made outside the trunk
Day-to-day operations documents afc patch reset-to-origin and refs/hub/replaced/*
the API reference summary table lists the reset-to-origin endpoint
the afc workspace sync CLI reference no longer claims origin is never fetched by sync
tests.pseudocode: doc = readFile('docs/carry_patch_workflow.md'); assert 'PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin' in section('Getting Started'); assert 'reset-to-origin' in section('Resolving conflicts after a failed rebuild'); assert 'reset-to-origin' in section('Day-to-day operations'); assert 'reset-to-origin' in section('API reference'); assert 'never fetched by sync' not in doc

tests.title: docs/cli.md documents --fail-on-diverged/exit code 3 and a new afc patch reset-to-origin section

tests.title: docs/api.md and docs/openapi.yaml describe reset-to-origin and replaced_sha

tests.title: ADR 01's status is Accepted

tests.title: an operator recovers a discarded tip after manually resetting a diverged patch branch to the fork's tip
given: a running hub API and git server backed by a real database and real git repositories
a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report, synced once and reporting the patch branch in patches_diverged
tests.when: an operator calls POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin, then runs a plain git fetch against refs/hub/replaced/<branch>
then: the endpoint returns 200 with replaced_sha set to the discarded local tip

tests.title: an operator resets a patch via the CLI and confirms the backup is visible on the patch-status dashboard
given: a running hub API and CLI binary
a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and a diverged patch branch

then: the CLI exits 0 and prints the returned patch JSON
the dashboard entry for that patch carries replaced_sha equal to the tip of refs/hub/replaced/<branch>

tests.title: the backup namespace refuses a push and is cleaned up when its owning patch is removed
given: a running hub git server
a workspace with an existing refs/hub/replaced/<branch> ref belonging to a registered patch
tests.when: a developer attempts to push a ref under refs/hub/replaced/* directly, then an operator runs afc patch remove <workspace-slug> <patch-id> to hard-delete the owning patch

tests.title: a scheduler detects a diverged sync via exit code 3 and an operator resolves it with reset-to-origin
given: a running hub API and CLI binary
a carry_patch workspace under PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report with a patch branch that has diverged from origin
tests.when: a scheduler runs afc workspace sync <slug> --fail-on-diverged, observes exit code 3, and an operator then runs afc patch reset-to-origin <slug> <patch-id>
then: the sync command exits 3 and the sync response's patches_diverged array names the branch
the follow-up reset-to-origin call returns 200 and the branch is no longer diverged from origin on a subsequent sync
